plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation by cutting high-risk assets.
It builds a cash buffer and focuses on income and broad market exposure.
Expect lower volatility and a more stable equity curve.
conservative.read: This mode aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged positions and holding a larger cash buffer. Drawdowns should be minimal.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU) to low single digits.
Trim SPY to 25% to balance broad index exposure.
Buy TZA (inverse ETF) for a small hedge against market downturns.
This plan seeks risk-first growth by blending broad markets with reduced leverage.
It maintains a moderate cash buffer and aims for steady gains.
Expect moderate volatility and a balanced risk/reward profile.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets approximately 2.5% per month with a focus on risk management. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a small hedging position. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU) up to 6% each.
Trim SPY to 15% to concentrate capital in higher-conviction areas.
Buy SOXS (inverse ETF) to capitalize on potential tech/semiconductor weakness.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by concentrating in leveraged plays.
It accepts higher volatility and potential for larger drawdowns.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk and leverage decay.
aggressive.read: This aggressive mode targets around 4% per month, accepting significantly higher risk and potential drawdowns. It concentrates capital in leveraged ETFs and high-conviction names, with a smaller cash buffer. Leverage decay in ETFs is a key risk.

plan: Sell all leveraged and high-beta single names (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income-generating asset allocation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income and capital preservation.
It shifts the portfolio towards income-focused ETFs and away from volatile growth assets.
Expect low growth but a more stable NAV with regular distributions.
Distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
income.read: This income-focused mode targets around 1% per month, prioritizing steady distributions and low drawdowns. It eliminates leverage and high-beta single names, concentrating on income-generating ETFs. While aiming for stability, NAV can still fall in market downturns.
